newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: TENNIS-NOVOTNA MAY NOT HAVE THE STOMACH FOR FED CUP TIE.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-NOVOTNA MAY NOT HAVE THE STOMACH FOR FED CUP TIE.

text.p: Wimbledon runner-up Jana Novtona aims to lead the Czech Republic to victory against the Netherlands in their Fed Cup semifinal this weekend, but she may have to rely heavily on an inexperienced supporting cast because of a nagging stomach injury.

Novotna, who reached a career high ranking of number two following Wimbledon has been hampered recently by a pulled stomach muscle, a problem exacerbated by a tense, three-set Wimbledon final against Martina Hingis.

On Thursday she attempted to serve for the first time since her loss at the All England Club last Saturday, but non-playing team captain Hana Mandlikova said she would wait until Saturday to name her opening singles lineup.
"I will do everything to prepare for the weekend and believe that I will be ready," Novotna said.

If not, Mandlikova will be forced to rely upon Adriana Gersi, Sandra Kleinova and Eva Martincova, just as she did against an injury-hit German team in the previous round last March when Novotna was also out of action due to illness.
"We are prepared to do whatever we can to get Jana on the court. If she can't, then the three others will have to pick up the lead," Mandlikova, winner of four Grand Slam titles, said.
Either way, Dutch captain Fred Hemmes, who watched his squad upset the American defending champions in March, is taking no chances in preparing his players to face a tough home team challenge.

Hemmes has chosen Brenda Schultz-McCarthy, Miriam Oremans, Kristie Boogert and Manon Bollegraf to lead the Netherlands on the clay courts of Prague's Stvanice Stadium, and said he expected Novotna to play.
"I saw Jana and how she looked when she came here, and to me she looked healthy overall," he said.
